bugs.explanation: Without `<!DOCTYPE html>`, browsers enter quirks mode which emulates old buggy behavior. Always start HTML5 documents with `<!DOCTYPE html>` as the very first line.

The `lang` attribute on `<html>` tells browsers and screen readers the language of the page. Omitting it hinders accessibility (screen readers may mispronounce content) and hurts SEO. Always specify `lang`.
Without `<meta charset="UTF-8">`, the browser may misinterpret character encoding, garbling special characters. Always declare the charset early in `<head>`.

Without the viewport meta tag, mobile browsers render the page at desktop width and scale it down, making the site appear zoomed out. Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.

Nesting `<a>` inside another `<a>` is invalid HTML — interactive elements cannot be nested. Browsers will attempt to repair the markup, often with unexpected results. Restructure to have sibling links.

Alt text should describe the image meaningfully, not describe it as decorative in the alt itself. For purely decorative images use `alt=""` (empty). For meaningful images, provide a concise description of what the image conveys.

Without an explicit `type`, a `<button>` inside a form defaults to `type="submit"`, which is usually intended but should be explicit. If the button is not a submit button (e.g., it runs JavaScript), use `type="button"` to prevent accidental form submission.

A `<label>` without a `for` attribute (matching an input's `id`) or wrapping the input is not programmatically associated. Screen readers can't announce which label belongs to which control. Use `for`/`id` pairing or wrap the input inside the label.

An `<input>` without a `type` attribute defaults to `type="text"`, which is usually what is intended. However, always be explicit — omitting `type` makes the intent unclear and may differ across browsers for exotic input types.
Using `<td>` for header cells and omitting `<thead>`/`<tbody>` makes tables inaccessible. Use `<th>` with `scope` for header cells and wrap rows in `<thead>` and `<tbody>` for semantic structure.

`id` values must be unique within a document. Duplicate IDs cause CSS and JavaScript targeting issues, break anchor navigation, and fail accessibility requirements. Use unique IDs or switch to classes for shared styling.
Skipping heading levels (h1 → h3) breaks the document outline and confuses screen reader users who navigate by heading. Use heading levels sequentially without skipping.

A page should have only one `<h1>` as the primary heading for the page or main content. Multiple `<h1>` elements make the document hierarchy unclear for both search engines and assistive technologies.
Without explicit `value` attributes, the form submits the option's text content, which is fragile (spacing/capitalization issues). Always add explicit `value` attributes to `<option>` elements.

title: fieldset and legend for Groups
code:
Gender:

Male Female

bugs.fix:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Gender</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="gender" value="m"> Male</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="gender" value="f"> Female</label>
</fieldset>
bugs.explanation: Radio buttons are a group and need a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` to provide context. Without it, screen readers announce each radio in isolation without indicating they belong to a group. Wrap groups in `<fieldset>/<legend>`.

bugs.fix:
<!-- Move to before </body> or add defer attribute -->
<script src="app.js" defer></script>
bugs.explanation: Scripts in `<head>` without `defer` or `async` block HTML parsing while they download and execute. Add `defer` (executes after parsing) or move the script tag to just before `</body>`. `defer` is generally preferred.

Without explicit `width` and `height`, the browser doesn't know the image size until it loads, causing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) as content reflows. Specifying dimensions lets the browser reserve space before the image loads.

An `<a>` without an `href` is not a link — it's just styled text. It is not keyboard-focusable and screen readers do not announce it as a link. Either add a valid `href` or use a `<button>` if the action is JavaScript-driven.

`target="_blank"` without `rel="noopener noreferrer"` allows the opened page to access the opener's `window` object via `window.opener`, enabling phishing attacks. Always add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to external `_blank` links.
